findings.description: AC-7's shadow-mode vacuity guard is insufficient for the mutation-identity-missing half of AC-2, and the Rationale's 'live not dormant' argument never establishes that half. AC-2 requires that a mutation-identity-missing rejection be distinguishable from a driver-lease-failure rejection, so a conforming test must actually reach a mutation-identity-missing REJECTION. But in the !identity branch the function does not return false — it returns `runtime.admission.mode !== 'server'`, i.e. it ACCEPTS (returns true) whenever admission.mode is 'none' or 'legacy', while still recording the blocker. A rejection on that cause therefore needs shadow mode AND admission.mode === 'server'. AC-7 names only `retained.mode === 'shadow'`, so a test built exactly to AC-7 can observe acceptance instead of rejection and leave AC-2 half-vacuous — the very failure mode AC-7 was added to prevent. Correspondingly, the Rationale's effectivity paragraph proves only that shadow mode always holds in production (via attachProductionTerminalAuthority -> setRetainedTerminalShadowEnabled(true)); it offers no evidence that admission.mode reaches 'server' in production, so the claim that BOTH rejection causes are live is unproven for mutation-identity-missing. The driver-lease-failure half is fully live and testable under shadow mode alone, so the requirement remains implementable — hence MEDIUM, not HIGH. Note OBS-BGSTAB-007 AC-7 is NOT affected: its AC-1/AC-2 need only some rejection, reachable via driver-lease-failure in shadow mode.

findings.description: The cause-1 attribution is incomplete in the same way the cause-2 attribution was before the last two rounds fixed it. The Requirement body labels cause 1 as '마운트되지 않은 StatusBar' and Implementation Notes contrast cause 2 as '마운트 수준의 국소 수정이 아니라 pane split 기능 전체의 구현' — which implies cause 1 IS a mount-level local fix. It is not. TC-6601 and TC-6606 both begin with pressCtrlB, and frontend/src contains no Ctrl+B key handler at all (no `key === 'b'` anywhere; the built-in shortcut profile defines only Shift+Enter, Ctrl+J and Enter) and nothing ever sets prefixMode — it exists solely as an unused StatusBar prop. TC-6606 further requires a ~1500 ms prefix auto-exit timer (it waits 1600 ms and asserts .status-prefix has disappeared). So disposition A for cause 1 requires mounting StatusBar PLUS a new Ctrl+B prefix-mode state machine PLUS an auto-exit timer. AC-4 demands only that StatusBar be reachable from the app tree and that a prefixMode supplier exist outside StatusBar.tsx; AC-8, which does enumerate extra required elements, is scoped to the cause-2 tests ('처분 A 를 택한 테스트가 `.pane-leaf` 외에 추가 요소를 요구하는 경우'). An implementer can therefore mount StatusBar, wire any prefixMode supplier, satisfy AC-4 in full, and still leave TC-6601 and TC-6606 RED. AC-2 (zero failures) remains an absolute backstop, so this is a scoping/checklist defect rather than an unachievable requirement — hence MEDIUM.

findings.description: The enumeration of fit trigger points is both internally inconsistent and incomplete. (a) The Rationale asserts '현재 구현은 네 트리거 지점 모두 0-size 를 감지하면 fit_skipped_non_renderable 이벤트만 남기고 재시도 스케줄 없이 return 한다', but the fourth cited site — the imperative fit() handle — performs NO dimension check whatsoever: it tests only `isVisibleRef.current` and then forwards to submitTerminalFit, which likewise has no dimension guard. So there is no zero-size detection to speak of at that site, and it emits no fit_skipped_non_renderable event. The block's own AC-3 gets this right (it frames the imperative case as '비가시 상태로 인해', i.e. invisibility, not zero size), so the Rationale contradicts its own acceptance criterion. (b) A fifth trigger point with a genuine zero-size skip is omitted from both the Requirement's '네 개의 fit 트리거 지점' enumeration and the Trace Links: performRepairLayout carries the same `container.offsetWidth === 0 || container.offsetHeight === 0` guard emitting fit_skipped_non_renderable, and it is arguably the worst instance because it calls resolve(true) — reporting SUCCESS to its caller — after skipping the fit. Only three of the four cited sites (3863, 4113, 4307) actually match the described pattern; the real fourth is 1191, not the imperative handle. An implementation that converges exactly the four enumerated sites would leave the repair-layout path permanently unconverged, which is the precise defect this requirement exists to close. The generic AC-1/AC-2/AC-4 wording does not name sites, so the barrier could still be fixed centrally — hence MEDIUM, not HIGH.

None changes a normative claim; all are reader-orientation defects. REL-BGSTAB-016: 'submitCapturedInputDirect observe-mode drop branch (897-940, drop at 915-932)' — the function actually spans 897-957 (the cited end lands mid-statement inside the second rejection path) and the observe drop branch opens at 917 and closes at 933 (915 is the shared `const mode = ...`, 916 the transient-blocked guard, 925-932 the returned literal). Same block: 'reusable toast pattern at 382-391, 1230-1235, 4435' — only 382 and 390 of that range belong to the pattern (383-389 are unrelated refs), and the show/auto-dismiss logic runs 1230-1236 (1236 closes the setTimeout); 4435 is exact. REL-BGSTAB-017: the ResizeObserver callback ends at 4142, not 4145 (4143-4145 are the comment and two .observe() calls), and the imperative fit handle is 2991-2997, not 2991-2996. REL-BGSTAB-018: 'reason mapping flattens every non-replay-pending code to server-error (4537-4556)' — the flattening is a single inline ternary at 4554 inside the method submitWebSocketInputThroughGateway (4511-4556); 4537-4538 are the replay-barrier computation, so the cited range is loose rather than wrong (it does contain 4554), and the behavioral claim is fully verified. OPS-BGSTAB-002: the wave3-terminal-authority-fairness row says the spec 'asserts helperDisabled false only (1320-1337)' but the toEqual at 1324-1328 asserts three fields (terminalSnapshotPresent, helperDisabled, helperReadOnly); and the terminal-keyboard-regression row describes the poll at 750-769 as asserting four fields when it asserts six — it additionally pins transportReady: false and barrierReason: 'repair-server-not-ready', i.e. the control is a transient-blocked state rather than a fully-ready one. AC-4 only requires captureAllowed true with both signals not disabled, all three of which that poll does assert, so it remains a valid control.

AC-1 reads '컨테이너가 0×0 이어서 fit 이 skip 되면, 추가 ResizeObserver 이벤트 없이도 geometryReadyRef 가 true 로 수렴하는 bounded 재시도 경로가 존재해야 한다'. Taken literally this is unsatisfiable in the sub-case where the container remains 0×0 forever — no retry can make the barrier legitimately ready — and it then sits in tension with AC-4, which requires a bounded retry to terminate with an observable signal. The Verification Method disambiguates the intent ('fit 경로를 0×0 에서 비-0 으로 전이시키되 ResizeObserver 이벤트를 발생시키지 않고'), i.e. the container does regain non-zero size and the retry re-measures without an RO event. Folding that precondition into AC-1 itself would remove the ambiguity. Pre-existing wording, not introduced by the last round.
